record.paper_title: Supernomial Coefficients, Bailey's Lemma and Rogers-Ramanujan-Type Identities. A Survey of Results and Open Problems
record.original_question: Develop an arbitrary-rank A_{n-1} version of the Bailey-type summations that include the A1 q-binomial invariance sum and the two A2 supernomial summations used to iterate identities. In this setting S(L,k) denotes the normalized A_{n-1} supernomial with L in Z_+^{n-1}, k in Z^n, and |k|=0. The desired arbitrary-rank theorem should be strong enough to iterate identities, not merely the known weak form sum_{L in Z_+^{n-1}} q^(L C L/2) S(L,k) = q^((k1^2+...+kn^2)/2)/(q)_infinity^{n-1}, because that weak form produces a new q-series identity but cannot be iterated indefinitely.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For each integer $n\geq 2$, the normalized $A_{n-1}$ supernomial coefficient $S(L,k)$ is a $q$-series-valued function of $L=(L_1,\dots,L_{n-1})\in\mathbb{Z}_{+}^{n-1}$ and $k=(k_1,\dots,k_n)\in\mathbb{Z}^{n}$ subject to $|k|:=k_1+\cdots+k_n=0$; for $n=2$ it reduces to the usual normalized $q$-binomial coefficient, and for $n=3$ it coincides with the $A_2$ supernomial. Let $C=(C_{ij})$ denote the Cartan matrix of $A_{n-1}$ and write $LCL = \sum_{i,j} C_{ij} L_i L_j$. The "weak" $A_{n-1}$ summation
$$\sum_{L\in\mathbb{Z}_{+}^{n-1}} q^{LCL/2}\, S(L,k) \;=\; \frac{q^{(k_1^2+\cdots+k_n^2)/2}}{(q;q)_\infty^{\,n-1}}$$
is known but is insufficient to iterate Bailey-type chains of identities.

Problem. Find and prove an arbitrary-rank $A_{n-1}$ Bailey-type summation theorem involving the supernomials $S(L,k)$ that simultaneously generalizes:
(i) the $A_1$ $q$-binomial invariance summation, and
(ii) the two known $A_2$ supernomial summations used in the Bailey iteration,
and is strong enough to admit indefinite iteration, thereby producing infinite families of Rogers–Ramanujan-type identities of higher rank rather than only the single identity yielded by the weak form above.
artifact.status_search_result: Surveys on Bailey's lemma and supernomial coefficients (Warnaar, "50 Years of Bailey's Lemma", and the supernomial survey itself) describe the iterable $A_{n-1}$ generalization of the $A_2$ supernomial Bailey summations as an open problem; only the weak (non-iterable) $A_{n-1}$ summation and the $A_2$ iterable case are known. No subsequent publication establishing the iterable arbitrary-rank version was located.

status_evidence.title: 50 Years of Bailey's Lemma
status_evidence.snippet: Unsolved problems of supernomial inversion, A_{n-1} and higher level extensions yield new results and conjectures involving A_{n-1} basic hypergeometric series.
status_evidence.claim: Higher-rank A_{n-1} supernomial extensions of Bailey's lemma are listed among unsolved problems.

status_evidence.title: Supernomial Coefficients, Bailey's Lemma and Rogers–Ramanujan-type Identities (survey)
status_evidence.snippet: generalizing theorem to A_{n-1} ... one cannot iterate ad infinitum
status_evidence.claim: The author records the iterable A_{n-1} generalization as an open problem, noting the known weak A_{n-1} sum cannot be iterated indefinitely.
